hook: Karen Spärck Jones studied history and moral sciences at Girton College, Cambridge, then turned to natural language processing and information retrieval, joining the Cambridge Language Research Unit and later the Computer Laboratory at the University of Cambridge. In 1972 she published A Statistical Interpretation of Term Specificity and Its Application in Retrieval, introducing inverse document frequency as a way to weight how informative a word is across a document collection. IDF became one half of TF-IDF, the weighting scheme that underpinned search engines for decades and remains a building block of modern text retrieval and vector search systems. She spent her career at Cambridge, served as president of the Association for Computational Linguistics, and was an outspoken advocate for women in computing.
name: Karen Spärck Jones

quote.text: Computing is too important to be left to men.
quote.context: A remark she made repeatedly in interviews and talks encouraging more women to enter computing research.

timeline.event: Begins studying at Girton College, Cambridge
timeline.impact: Trained in history and moral sciences before moving into computational research.

timeline.event: Publishes A Statistical Interpretation of Term Specificity and Its Application in Retrieval
timeline.impact: Introduced inverse document frequency, later combined with term frequency into the TF-IDF weighting scheme used across search and retrieval systems.

timeline.event: Serves as President of the Association for Computational Linguistics
timeline.impact: Provided leadership to the field's primary academic society.

timeline.event: Receives the ACL Lifetime Achievement Award
timeline.impact: Recognized for her foundational contributions to computational linguistics and information retrieval.

timeline.impact: Closed a career that shaped the mathematical foundations of modern search.

quick_facts: Studied history and moral sciences at Girton College, Cambridge
Introduced inverse document frequency in a 1972 paper
IDF is one of the two components of TF-IDF, a foundational text-weighting scheme
President of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 1994
Won the ACL Lifetime Achievement Award and the BCS Lovelace Medal, both in 2004 and 2007 respectively

achievements.title: Inverse document frequency
achievements.impact: Provided a statistical way to weight terms by how much information they carry across a collection, becoming the second half of TF-IDF and a foundation of modern search and retrieval ranking.

achievements.title: Probabilistic models of information retrieval
achievements.impact: Contributed to the probabilistic relevance framework that shaped decades of search engine ranking research.

achievements.title: Advocacy for women in computing
achievements.impact: Used her prominence in the field to push for greater representation of women in computer science research.
